decision: Keep the default-off prototype isolated. Two opposite-order clean pairs do not establish consistent net FPS/1%-low improvement. Product core remains Stage3 b3b; do not enable or promote.

limitations: Frozen full-frame pixel oracle, not FPS/GPU-time evidence. No geometry/source absence control is needed because candidate changes resolve ownership only.
Counts are actual gl.blitFramebuffer API calls/masks, not proof of driver allocation, bytes or implicit automatic resolves.
Working framebuffer/reflection/postprocess targets are overwritten; a normal original-mode native refresh is checked after restoration.
Exposure histories/controls are restored. Material versions/program dirtiness are not rolled back. GL errors are consumed/reported and cannot be requeued.
Native renderer.resetState invalidates private caches; raw framebuffer/drawBuffers/buffer bindings are not replayed. Synchronous controlled QA only.

limits: Explicit full-frame color/depth blit counts are not GPU time or bandwidth measurements.
Same draw count and strict four-view pixel equality establish the controlled tested cases, not arbitrary custom callbacks, added layer2 objects or all future shaders.

All four paired runs disable common passive longtask/long-animation-frame observers and per-pass diagnostics. Earlier isolated readings may retain those common observers; do not attribute cross-harness changes to the candidate.
Paired comparisons still use the same legacy RAF completion polling; a separate loop-observation experiment uses interval polling and is not mixed into these pairs.
The second pair reversed candidate/baseline order. Complete 1% lows include all long frames; warm windows are supplemental.
Render-submission intervals are not physical presents. The target remains unmet.
